test_title: SSC MTS 2024 Official Paper (Held On: 04 Nov, 2024 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: How many central banks can a country have?
solution:
The Correct answer is __**One**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **central bank** is a national institution responsible for managing the **currency, monetary policy, and financial stability** of a country.
 
• Most countries have **one central bank** to ensure a centralized authority managing monetary policy and to avoid conflicts in economic strategies.
 
• The central bank acts as a regulator of commercial banks, ensuring the **stability of the banking system**.
 
• In India, the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** is the central bank, established in **1935** under the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934.
 
• Central banks issue **currency**, control inflation, and ensure smooth economic functioning by implementing **monetary policies**.
 
• They play a crucial role in maintaining the **foreign exchange reserve** and stabilizing the national economy in times of crisis.
 
• The central bank serves as the **lender of last resort** to commercial banks during financial distress.
 
• Examples of central banks include the **Federal Reserve** in the United States, the **European Central Bank**, and the **Bank of England**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Four**__

 __
 
• Having multiple central banks in a single country can lead to **confusion and conflicts** in monetary policies.
 
• It would result in lack of **uniformity** in managing inflation, interest rates, and currency stability.
 
 
 
• **Three**__
 __
 
• Similar to having four central banks, having three would create **overlapping functions** and dilute the efficiency of economic management.
 
 
 
• **Two**__
 
 
• Some countries have dual monetary systems for specific reasons, but this is not common as it complicates **policy implementation**.
 
• For example, Hong Kong and Macau both have monetary authorities but operate under special circumstances.
